newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs seen steady to higher, pork bellies mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs seen steady to higher, pork bellies mixed.

text.p: CME hog futures were expected to open steady to 0.200 cent per lb higher while calls ranged mixed, from 0.200 cent a lb lower to 0.200 higher for pork belly futures, livestock analysts said.

Hog futures are seen up on further gains in cash hog prices linked to good packer demand and higher pork cutout values. Hot and humid weather also continued to restrict hog marketings in some areas of the Midwest, analysts said.
However, back months could again show resistance ahead of Friday's quarterly USDA Hogs and Pigs Report which is expected to show expansion of the hog herd, sources said.

Early analysts' estimates on Friday's USDA report put all hogs on U.S. farms as of June 1 at 101.7 to 104 percent of last year. Kept for breeding numbers were ranging from 103 to 106 percent and kept for market 101 to 105 percent.

Pork belly indications ranged mixed as some analysts look for further pressure ahead of the CME Out-of-Town Report Tuesday afternoon. The report could show a net in-movement last week versus an out-movement last year, they said.
However, other analysts look for support, owing to firmer cash belly prices
USDA quoted 12- to 14-lb bellies up $2.00 at $81.00 per cwt.
Spreading ahead of the USDA hog report is also likely, some sources noted.
